standard.title: Sourcing Requirements for Disseminated Analytic Products
standard.summary: Every covered analytic product shall contain sourcing information so readers can assess the quality and credibility of sources and locate the originals. Sourcing is presented through four mechanisms: Source Reference Citations, Appended Reference Citations, Source Descriptors, and Source Summary Statements. Analysts should combine these mechanisms to optimise clarity.

mechanism.name: Source Reference Citation (SRC)
mechanism.description: Sequentially numbered endnotes that correlate to superscript numbers in the body of the analytic product.
mechanism.generated-when: A source is directly cited in the product text, or a specific aspect of analysis (judgment, assessment, estimate, alternative hypothesis, or confidence level) depends on a source.

rules.rule: Reference the most original source that presents the relevant information in a form appropriate for analysis.
The relevance of a source should be apparent if a reader consults it directly; otherwise the product text must explain the source's pertinence.
Do not use an SRC for information that only meets the criteria for an Appended Reference Citation and is not directly cited in the text.

elements.element: identification of the information originator, author, producer, or owner
an unambiguous source identifier enabling efficient location and retrieval
a title (with volume/issue number if applicable, and title classification if included)
date of issuance, publication, or posting (or date of online access if unknown)
overall classification of the source document
a source descriptor (optional if included in the main body; if different, the portion marking must still be included)

mechanism.name: Appended Reference Citation (ARC)
mechanism.description: For information that relates to analysis in a supplemental or complementary way but does not expressly affect or support a specific aspect or outcome of analysis.

rules.rule: Do not include ARCs solely to delineate the overall scope of analytic inquiry.
If included, list ARCs separately from and after SRCs.

elements.element: source identifying, labelling, or tagging information (if the reference is accessible)
a succinct explanation for its inclusion

mechanism.name: Source Descriptor
mechanism.description: A brief narrative about factors affecting the quality or credibility of a single source (accuracy, completeness, potential bias, relevance, etc.). It should appear in the main body; if not, it shall appear in the SRC. Use a source descriptor to describe qualitative factors germane to specific judgments, or when the time of the pertinent information differs significantly from the time of publication.

rules.rule: For intelligence-based or diplomatic sources, derive the descriptor from source documents; indicate any substantial changes and the rationale.
Analysts may devise descriptors for publicly available information not obtained from an IC-produced open-source report.
For a directly-cited source, the descriptor should also appear in the text, clearly associated with the source.

mechanism.name: Source Summary Statement
mechanism.description: A holistic assessment of the sourcing that supports the product as a whole. Importance increases with product complexity, source complexity, or the number of sources cited.

coverage.item: Strengths and weaknesses of the source base
Which sources are most critical to key judgments
Sources that are corroborative or conflicting

retention.rule: For sources that are dynamic (e.g. Internet posting), ephemeral (e.g. analyst phone conversation), or not subject to systematic storage, preserve a record of the source for at least one year.
For products with a specified time horizon, retain source information for the time horizon or five years, whichever is shorter.
Retain the covered analytic product, with all sourcing information, as a document of record, along with any downgraded, sanitised, or tearline versions.

glossary.definition: A subset of disseminated analytic products, designated by IC elements, that fall under the authority of ICD 206.

Any intelligence product (assessment, study, estimate, compilation, database, graphic, or interactive publication) created by the analytic component of an IC element, validated by that element, and disseminated to consumers outside the element.

An originator or discrete parcel of data or information that contributes to, affects, or is used to evaluate intelligence analysis. A source can be a person, document, quotation, data record, database, tweet, email, book, web page, etc.
A specified set of factual information elements about a source, presented in uniform format in an endnote, enabling readers to locate, retrieve, and assess the source.
Descriptive elements about information that relates to analysis in a supplemental way but does not expressly affect or support a specific outcome of analysis.
A brief narrative about factors affecting a single source's quality or credibility, distinct from the information elements in an SRC.
An explanation of quality, credibility, or validity factors pertaining to the entire set of sources on which a product is based.
The combined set of SRCs, ARCs, source descriptors, and source summary statements presented in a covered analytic product.
